pages.text: Between hosts, an infection is bookkeeping. Split a population into susceptible S, infected I and recovered: dI/dt = βSI/N − (γ + μ)I. At the start everyone is susceptible, and the infection grows only if each case makes more than one more: $(thing)R₀ = β/(γ + μ) > 1$(). Once a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ is immune, it can no longer spread.

That threshold is a $(thing)phase transition$(). Let each link of a network pass the infection with probability T: below a critical T, outbreaks stay small; above it a giant connected cluster appears and the infection $(thing)percolates$() through the whole population - like water through ground coffee, or a magnet ordering below its Curie point. On networks with hubs the critical T can be very small.
In the $(item)Holographic Encoder$(), a replicator, a resistant clone and a holographic matrix write the $(item)Contagion Network Map$(): every path an anomaly can take, and where R crosses 1.
Every contact, every transmission, every node an infection passed through. Somewhere in it is the threshold where R crosses 1.$(br2)Made in $(item)Holographic Encoder$().
